title: MZ How to write event contents in javascript in a separate js file

posts.author: virtuoussinner
Andar
posts.body:
Can you please take two steps back and explain why you want to do it this way?
There have been others who considered this for various reasons, but there is a big problem due to some of the event commands being asynchronous and/or linked to the main game loop differently.
One of the prime examples for this is the call common event command - it doesn't really exist as a javascript command. Even in the list of the javascript equivalents it only gives a function called "reservecommonevent" - because the common event can't be directly called by javascript, it can only push the CE into the reserve-line to be executed when the game engine decides it can execute it, but not at the same moment.
So most people rather go the clone event route: creating the events in a special map and copy them from there to whereever the event is needed at runtime.
There are other options as well, but we need to know the details on how and where and when you want to use the events stored that way.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Your example seems perfectly suited to the
Common Event
command:
Determine random NPC dialogue "type": Control Variables -> Set -> Random.
Branch their dialogue based on that variable: Conditional Branch -> Variable.
I don't recall ever seeing an example where generating event contents programmatically was the easier option.
All the usual sequence/wait stuff is courtesy of the corresponding interpreter instance (
Game_Interpreter
): it handles running one command after another; it decides when to proceed, or when to wait. It operates based on event commands (anonymous objects), like parcels being carried on a conveyor belt.
Like Andar says: the Common Event command just creates a new child interpreter and populates it with a ready-made event. It still uses the same basic event/interpreter structure, much like the classic "clone map event" approach.
The Event Code sheet of the RPG Maker MZ Script Call Reference documents RM's event p-code:
RPG Maker MZ Data and Script Call Reference
RPG Maker MZ Data and Script Call Reference  A collection of data and script calls for certain functions of RPG Maker MZ.   Supplementary Material:  Most of the script calls found in RPG Maker MV also works. If you want samples and notes to compare side by side. Please visit this topic...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
This is the same as the event code found in map files from your project's
data
subfolder. During play it gets fed into a relevant
Game_Interpreter
instance, which processes it accordingly (cf
Game_Interpreter
methods
update
and
executeCommand
in rmmz_objects.js).
For completeness, here's a link to the MV / MZ Script Call List:
RPG Maker MV / MZ Script Call List
This Script Call list applies to both RPG Maker MV and RPG Maker MZ. Link here to see the entire list.    Supplementary Material for RPG Maker MZ: https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/rpg-maker-mz-script-call-reference.122501/  Have fun eventing~
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
I recommend referring to the first/main sheet unless you cannot find something on there; Ctrl+F is your friend. E.g. you'll notice that the Show Choices call includes this line at the end:
JavaScript:
interpreter.setWaitMode('message')
That's the kind of "interpreter wait" mechanic I was yapping about.

posts.author: virtuoussinner
posts.body:
Thanks for the replies.
I wanted to do it this way to make the events modular and use Javascript's flexibility. Moreover, I want to do it in separate files so that I can reuse the events. Like my meetRandomBoy function, I can create any number of events in the same or different maps and call that function. If I do it from the script command, it will be limited to that function. In this way, I will not need to create common events.
I am not using the
JavaScript:
interpreter.setWaitMode('message')
because this line only works when called inside the script command, not when called from a separate file. You can see from my code that to overcome this issue, I created the
JavaScript:
waitForMessageCompletion
function that will stop the flow till the user clicks only then the second message will be displayed.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
virtuoussinner said:
I wanted to do it this way to make the events modular and use Javascript's flexibility.
Click to expand...
That doesn't really seem like a compelling reason to give up all of the convenience and built-in functionality of events.
Events can be modular by calling other events, just like JavaScript calls other functions; and you can still make use of variable and switches. You can even make a few Control Variables or Conditional Branches use the Script field and it will still be much easier than trying to code the entire thing.
virtuoussinner said:
Moreover, I want to do it in separate files so that I can reuse the events.
Click to expand...
I'm not sure what this means. If you're reusing them within a project, there's no difference between code in one file or separate files, and there's no reason you wouldn't be able to do it with events.
If you mean between different projects, you can open two projects and copy events between them quite easily.
Even the most proficient coders on this site (see above, caethyril
) recognize the value in when to use code and when not to.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
To add:
virtuoussinner said:
so that I can reuse the events
Click to expand...
MZ ships with a plugin called TemplateEvent. It's a "clone event" type plugin, like Andar mentioned. You can find it at:
<MZ install folder>/dlc/BasicResources/plugins/official/TemplateEvent.js
virtuoussinner said:
In this way, I will not need to create common events.
Click to expand...
A Common Event is essentially just one that is used in multiple places. And the existing interpreters operate based on events. So unless you want to reinvent the wheel here, you will need events in one form or another.
As I said, the engine's
Game_Interpreter
is a pretty standard queue/"conveyor belt" structure. It exists to control program flow, to achieve (amongst other things) exactly the sort of thing you're requesting:
caethyril said:
All the usual sequence/wait stuff is courtesy of the corresponding interpreter instance (
Game_Interpreter
): it handles running one command after another; it decides when to proceed, or when to wait. It operates based on event commands (anonymous objects), like parcels being carried on a conveyor belt.
Click to expand...
The p-code for event commands isn't pretty, but if you're set on creating events with code then you're gonna hafta deal with it.
virtuoussinner said:
You can see from my code that to overcome this issue, I created the
JavaScript:
waitForMessageCompletion
function that will stop the flow till the user clicks only then the second message will be displayed.
Click to expand...
Instead of which, you could use the existing engine structure to wait until the message is done, e.g. with an interpreter wait mode, or by patching into a relevant
update
method to perform a custom check every frame. Integrating into the existing system helps to reduce the occurrence of hard-to-debug errors and desync issues.
